items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I got Lee Young, who was Lester Young’s brother, playing drums with me.

ctx.x: Did you put him on lead then?

Yeah, he played lead. And I got Lee Young, who was Lester Young’s brother, playing drums with me. And I kept picking up men like that until I picked up a 16 piece band. And so I got some arrangements from a guy by the name of Joey Williams, who had a book of arrangements, and I got, and he was a terrific arranger. The first arrangement that, oh, what’s the big band leader’s name? What I’m going to tell you, you’re going to be shocked. Glenn Miller. This guy arranged for Glenn Miller. Because it wasn’t Glenn…
For the way the reed section worked?

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I liked working with Hamp's band... he really wanted Nat, but I had been to New York... Hampton just left Goodman, so when he come out -- he really wanted Nat, but I had been to New York... I think I stayed about 3 weeks... Lionel left Benny and he came back to the West Coast... I liked working with

ctx.x: Who was it you drove your bargain with? Who was it that agreed to your terms?

Well, George Estolle really agreed to them, you know, but we were in Mr. Mayer's office; I never will forget, because we went right in there, they took me right in the Big Man's office. And someone else was the Big Man there, Talmadge or something -- Norman Talmadge -- someone like that, but MGM was really the biggest studio in Hollywood then.

And so I did that with George Estolle and them --and it did launch me as a -- it helped me immensely in the studios. But after that, I think, was when Lionel Hampton came back with Benny Goodman, when he broke up in 1940; he came out here and he formed his band, and what he wanted for the rhythm section was Nat's trio and myself, you know. And all the young musicians then just loved big bands, you know, because that's what it was, you know; Andy Kirk, Benny, and Artie Shaw, Charlie Barnet, you know --Basie and…
